background: Bank of China (Hong Kong) is one of the three note-issuing banks in Hong Kong and the second-largest there, a subsidiary of Bank of China, funded by Hong Kong deposits and lending to local corporates, households and across Southeast Asia.
synthesis: Ratings are A+ from Fitch and S&P and Aa3 from Moody's, all stable, with Fitch's upgrade to A+ on 14 Nov 2024 the latest move. The ratios are the strongest among the Asian peers held here: CET1 of 24.1% is in the top quarter against the peer median, and LCR of 180% and NSFR of 143% are both in the top quarter. LCR has fallen 51 points since 31 Mar 2025, a big move from a very high level, while CET1 has risen 0.5 points. Nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days. The mainland parent is the main thing a depositor is exposed to beyond the figures.
